description: A collection of agent-cli improvements: local model support, error stream presentation, TODO subsystem for model continuation, refusal message parsing, media type handling with auto-conversion, skill loading commands, audio/image generation via completions API, and multi-session terminal visualization.

userStories.title: Add `local` provider type to config struct
userStories.description: As a developer running a local inference server, I want to configure a `local` provider with just a base URL and model name (no API key) so I can run agent-cli against local models without dummy credentials.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `ProviderLocal = "local"` constant to `internal/config/interface.go` provider enum
Add `BaseURL string` field to the provider config struct so local endpoints can be specified
`apiKey` is optional (empty string valid) when provider is `local`
Config validation in `internal/config/loading.go` skips API key requirement for `local` providers
Existing `openai` and `openrouter` providers still require `apiKey` (no regression)
Unit test covers: local provider with no API key passes validation, openai provider with no API key fails validation
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundational config change required by US-002. Files: internal/config/interface.go, internal/config/loading.go

userStories.title: Build inferencer without auth for local providers
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the OpenAI-compatible inferencer to omit the Authorization header when the provider is `local`, so local servers don't reject requests due to invalid auth tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: In `internal/agent/executor.go` BuildLoop(), detect `provider=local` and construct inferencer with no auth header
The existing `oaiprovider` / `gateway` stack is reused — no new HTTP client written
When provider is `local` and `baseURL` is set, the outgoing request uses `baseURL` as the endpoint base
Integration test: start an in-process mock HTTP server, configure agent with `provider=local, baseURL=<mock URL>`, assert no `Authorization` header in the request and response is parsed correctly
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, test/

userStories.title: Add `--base-url` CLI flag and `agent config add-local` command
userStories.description: As a power user, I want to override the provider to `local` via CLI flags, and as a new user I want a command to register a local provider in config without hand-editing YAML.
acceptanceCriteria: `--base-url <url>` flag added to `ask` and `chat` commands in `internal/cli/`
When `--provider local` and `--base-url` are both set, no API key is required and the request is routed to `<base-url>`
Error printed if `--provider local` is set without `--base-url`
New subcommand `agent config add-local --name <name> --base-url <url> --model <model>` writes a local provider entry to `~/.agent-cli/config.yaml`
If the URL is unreachable, a warning is printed but config is still saved
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001, US-002. Files: internal/cli/ask.go, internal/cli/chat.go, internal/cli/routes.go, internal/config/loading.go

userStories.title: Add ErrorCollector to RunData for centralized error routing
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a centralized error collector in the agent's RunData so all subsystems (tools, inference, session) can route errors to a single place, enabling consistent presentation across ask and chat commands.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `ErrorCollector` struct (or interface) to `internal/agent/` with `Add(source string, err error)` and `Errors() []CollectedError` methods
`CollectedError` has fields: `Source string` (e.g., `"tool:exec"`, `"inference:openrouter"`), `Message string`, `Time time.Time`
`ErrorCollector` is attached to `RunData` in `executor.go`
Tool registry errors in `internal/tools/registry.go` are routed to the collector instead of being returned inline
Inference errors in `ExecuteOneTurn()` are routed to the collector
Unit test: add 3 errors, assert `Errors()` returns all 3 with correct source tags
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundational for US-005 and US-006. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/tools/registry.go

userStories.title: Route errors to stderr with [ERROR] prefix in ask command
userStories.description: As a user running `agent ask`, I want errors to appear on stderr with a clear [ERROR] prefix so I can separate model output from error messages in scripts and pipelines.
acceptanceCriteria: All errors from the `ErrorCollector` are written to `os.Stderr` (not stdout) in `ask` command flow
Each error is prefixed with `[ERROR]` in plain text mode
When stderr is a TTY, prefix and message are colored red using ANSI codes
No color codes emitted when stderr is not a TTY (detect via `golang.org/x/term` `IsTerminal`)
In non-streaming mode, if any errors occurred, a `\n--- Session Errors ---\n` summary block is appended to stderr after output completes; omitted if no errors
Stdout contains only model output — piping `agent ask "..." > out.txt` captures no error text
Existing tests that assert stdout output are not broken
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/cli/ask.go, internal/output/

userStories.title: Route errors to stderr in chat command
userStories.description: As a user in an interactive chat session, I want errors (tool failures, inference errors) to appear on stderr with a clear [ERROR] prefix so they don't pollute the chat output.
acceptanceCriteria: All errors from the `ErrorCollector` are written to `os.Stderr` in `chat` command flow (same pattern as US-005)
Errors are displayed immediately as they occur (not only at session end) so the user sees them in real time
Chat prompt is re-displayed after an error so the user can continue the conversation
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004. Files: internal/cli/chat.go, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Structured JSON error output in --output-json mode
userStories.description: As a developer using `--output-json`, I want errors to be emitted as structured JSON objects on stderr so I can parse them programmatically.
acceptanceCriteria: When `--output-json` is active, each collected error is emitted to stderr as: `{"type":"error","source":"<source>","message":"<msg>","timestamp":"<ISO8601>"}`
Error JSON objects do NOT appear in the stdout NDJSON stream
Existing token/chunk JSON objects on stdout are unaffected
Integration test: run with `--output-json`, assert stdout parses cleanly as NDJSON and stderr contains valid error JSON
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-004, US-005. Files: internal/output/, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Define TodoQueue struct in agent loop state
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a TodoQueue struct stored in the agent loop's RunData so I can enqueue and dequeue todo items (operations to perform) during execution.
acceptanceCriteria: New `TodoQueue` type defined in `internal/agent/` as a FIFO queue of `TodoItem` structs
`TodoItem` has fields: `ID string`, `Description string`, `Done bool`
`TodoQueue` has methods: `Enqueue(description string) string` (returns ID), `MarkDone(id string)`, `Remaining() []TodoItem`, `All() []TodoItem`
`TodoQueue` is attached to `RunData` in `executor.go`
Unit tests: Enqueue 3 items, MarkDone 1, assert Remaining() returns 2 items; empty queue Remaining() returns empty slice
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundational for US-009. Files: internal/agent/executor.go (or new internal/agent/todo.go)

userStories.title: Parse todo items from model output and track completion
userStories.description: As the agent coordinator, I want to parse todo items from the model's output (lines starting with `- [ ]` or `TODO:`) and track their completion so I know whether the model has finished all its tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: After each `ExecuteOneTurn()`, scan the model's output text for patterns: `- [ ] <task>` (incomplete) and `- [x] <task>` (complete)
Incomplete items are enqueued into the `TodoQueue` if not already present (matched by description)
Complete items (`- [x]`) are marked done in the `TodoQueue`
Unit test: model output with 3 incomplete and 1 complete todo → queue has 3 remaining, 1 done
Unit test: model output with no todos → queue unchanged
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-008. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/agent/todo.go

userStories.title: Coordinator nudges model when remaining todos exist
userStories.description: As the agent coordinator, I want to re-invoke inference with a nudge message when the model completes its turn but the TodoQueue still has incomplete items, so tasks complete without manual intervention.
acceptanceCriteria: After `ExecuteOneTurn()` and todo parsing, if `TodoQueue.Remaining()` is non-empty, append a system message: `"You have <N> remaining todos: [<list>]. Please continue."` and re-invoke inference
Re-invocation loop continues until `Remaining()` is empty, stop-word is matched, or max nudge depth is reached
`maxNudgeDepth` is configurable in model config (default: 5); add the field to model config struct
If stop-word is matched, nudge is NOT triggered even if todos remain
Integration test: mock inferencer returns output with `- [ ] step1` on first call, `- [x] step1` on second; assert inference called exactly twice
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-008, US-009. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/config/interface.go

userStories.title: Add repetition penalty config field for small models
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to set a repetition penalty on a per-model basis in config so small models don't loop on the same output.
acceptanceCriteria: `repetitionPenalty float64` field added to model config struct in `internal/config/interface.go` (valid range 1.0–2.0, default 1.0 = disabled)
Field is passed through to the OpenAI-compatible inferencer request payload as `frequency_penalty` for OpenAI/OpenRouter providers
For `local` provider, field is passed as `repetition_penalty` in the request body
Config loading/saving handles the new field without breaking existing configs
Integration test: set `repetitionPenalty: 1.3`, assert the outgoing HTTP request body contains the correct penalty field
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Independent of todo queue. Files: internal/config/interface.go, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Parse `refusal` field from OpenAI API response
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the message parser to extract the `refusal` field from OpenAI-compatible responses so the agent is aware when a model has refused a request.
acceptanceCriteria: The assistant message struct includes a `Refusal string` field
The OpenAI response parser populates `Refusal` when the API response contains a non-empty `refusal` field
Refusal is treated as a distinct content type — not an error, not regular text content
In streaming mode, `delta.refusal` chunks are accumulated into the final `Refusal` field (parallel to content accumulation)
Unit test: parse mock API response with `"refusal": "I cannot assist with that."` → assert `Refusal` field populated, `Content` empty
Unit test: stream mock response with refusal deltas → assert accumulated refusal text is correct
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Files: messages package in llm-gateway, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Display refusal messages with [REFUSAL] prefix and store in session
userStories.description: As a user whose request was refused, I want to see a clear [REFUSAL] message so I know the model deliberately declined, and I want it stored in session history for later review.
acceptanceCriteria: When a refusal is detected, it is written to stderr with `[REFUSAL]` prefix immediately
When stderr is a TTY, refusal text is displayed in yellow ANSI color
No 'empty response' or confusing error is shown when a refusal is the only response
Refusal is stored in session history as a distinct message type so `agent session show` displays it with `[REFUSAL]` prefix
Exit code is `0` (refusal is a valid response, not a failure)
In `--output-json` mode, refusal is emitted to stderr as: `{"type":"refusal","message":"<text>","model":"<id>","timestamp":"<ISO8601>"}`
Integration test: mock inferencer returns refusal → assert stderr contains `[REFUSAL]`, stdout is empty, session JSON stores the refusal
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-012. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/output/, internal/session/storage.go

userStories.title: Add `supportedInputMimeTypes` to model config and populate registry
userStories.description: As a developer configuring a model, I want to specify which MIME types the model accepts as file inputs so the CLI can validate and auto-convert files before uploading.
acceptanceCriteria: `supportedInputMimeTypes []string` field added to model config struct in `internal/config/interface.go`
Field defaults to `nil` (meaning accept all) for backward compatibility
Default `models.yaml` registry updated with accurate MIME type lists for all pre-seeded models based on their API documentation (e.g., gpt-4o: image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp)
Config loading/saving handles the new field without breaking existing configs
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundational for US-015, US-016. Files: internal/config/interface.go, internal/config/models.go

userStories.title: MIME type detection and validation before file upload
userStories.description: As a user providing a file to the agent, I want to receive a clear error if the model doesn't support that file type so I know immediately rather than getting a silent failure from the API.
acceptanceCriteria: Before adding a file to the conversation, detect the MIME type using both file extension (`mime` package) and magic byte sniffing (`net/http.DetectContentType`, first 512 bytes)
WebP detection: check RIFF header (bytes 0-3) and WEBP marker (bytes 8-11)
If the model's `supportedInputMimeTypes` is non-empty and file MIME type is not in the list, validation fails with: `"Model '<model>' does not support input type '<mime>'. Supported types: <list>"`
Validation occurs in the input-preparation step (before any inference call)
If `supportedInputMimeTypes` is nil/empty, all types are accepted (no change to current behavior)
Unit tests: supported type passes, unsupported type fails, nil list passes, WebP correctly detected
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-014. Files: internal/input/, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Auto-convert unsupported image formats before upload
userStories.description: As a user whose file format isn't supported by the model, I want the CLI to automatically convert it to a supported format (e.g., WebP → PNG) so I don't have to manually convert files.
acceptanceCriteria: When a file fails MIME validation and a conversion path exists, attempt automatic conversion before returning an error
Conversion pairs supported: WebP → PNG, WebP → JPEG, TIFF → PNG, TIFF → JPEG
Use Go's `image` package + `golang.org/x/image` (WebP decoder) + `image/png` / `image/jpeg` for conversion
On successful conversion, use the converted file transparently and log to stderr: `"[INFO] Converted <original> (image/webp) → <tmp>.png (image/png) for model compatibility"`
On conversion failure, fall back to the original validation error message
Converted file is a temporary file (cleaned up after session ends)
Unit test: provide WebP bytes → assert PNG output bytes with correct PNG magic bytes `\x89PNG`
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-015. May need `golang.org/x/image` as a new dependency. Files: internal/input/

userStories.title: Add `--skills` flag to `ask` and `chat` commands
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want to specify one or more skills when invoking `agent ask` or `agent chat` so the agent starts with those skill instructions pre-loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: `--skills <name1,name2,...>` flag added to both `ask` and `chat` commands
Skills are loaded via the existing `skills.Loader` and their instructions are injected into the system prompt at session start (after existing skill summary injection)
Multiple skills are concatenated in the order specified
If a named skill is not found, the command fails with: `"Skill '<name>' not found. Available skills: <list>"`
Flag accepts both comma-separated (`--skills a,b`) and repeated (`--skills a --skills b`) forms
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Files: internal/cli/ask.go, internal/cli/chat.go, internal/flags/, internal/agent/executor.go

userStories.title: Add `/load <skill>` command in chat with tab autocomplete
userStories.description: As a user in an interactive chat session, I want to type `/load <skill-name>` to inject a skill's instructions into the current context so I can add capabilities mid-conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: Chat input pre-processor recognizes `/load <name>` as a special command and does NOT forward it to the model
Skill is resolved via `skills.Loader`; instructions are appended to the active session context for the next inference call
If skill not found: `"Skill '<name>' not found. Available: <list>"` printed to stderr
Tab completion on `/load ` shows all available skill names from the loader
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-017. Files: internal/cli/chat.go, internal/skills/loader.go

userStories.title: Add agent profiles to config and `agent load <profile>` command
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to define named agent profiles (model + provider + default skills) in config and launch them with `agent load <profile>` so I don't repeat flags for common setups.
acceptanceCriteria: New `agents` section in `~/.agent-cli/config.yaml` with array of profile objects: `{name, model, provider, skills: []}`
Config loading reads the `agents` section into a new `AgentProfile` struct slice in the config
`agent load <name>` new top-level command resolves the profile and starts an interactive chat with the specified model, provider, and skills pre-loaded
If profile not found: error message listing available profiles
Profile fields can be overridden by CLI flags (`--model`, `--provider`, `--skills`)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-017. Files: internal/config/interface.go, internal/config/loading.go, internal/cli/routes.go

userStories.title: Enhance `dispatch_agent` tool with skills, model, and provider params
userStories.description: As a model running in agent-cli, I want to dispatch a sub-agent with a specific set of skills and model so I can delegate specialized tasks to purpose-built sub-agents.
acceptanceCriteria: `dispatch_agent` tool JSON parameters schema extended with optional fields: `skills` (array of strings), `model` (string), `provider` (string)
When `skills` is provided, sub-agent process is launched with `--skills <names>` flag
When `model`/`provider` are provided, sub-agent process is launched with `--model`/`--provider` flags
Existing `dispatch_agent` calls without the new fields continue to work (backward compatible)
Tool schema in `internal/tools/tool_dispatch_agent.go` updated to reflect new parameters
Integration test: dispatch sub-agent with `skills=["translator"]` and assert the child process receives `--skills translator`
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-017. Files: internal/tools/tool_dispatch_agent.go

userStories.title: Add `--output-format` flag and binary stdout mode to `ask` command
userStories.description: As a user, I want to pipe raw binary output (image/audio) from agent-cli directly to a file so I can generate media without extra scripting.
acceptanceCriteria: `--output-format <mime>` flag added to `ask` command (e.g., `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `audio/wav`, `audio/mp3`)
When `--output-format` is a binary MIME type, stdout emits raw binary bytes only (no text, no NDJSON, no spinner)
All log output, errors, and progress are routed to stderr when in binary output mode
Binary mode is activated only for non-text MIME types; text/* types use normal output mode
Piping produces a valid file: `agent ask "generate image" --output-format image/png > out.png` (verified by file magic bytes)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundational for US-022, US-023. Files: internal/cli/ask.go, internal/agent/executor.go, internal/output/

userStories.title: Parse image content parts from chat completions response and emit as binary
userStories.description: As a developer, I want agent-cli to extract image data from chat completion responses (base64 image content parts) and write the raw bytes to stdout when `--output-format image/*` is set.
acceptanceCriteria: When `--output-format image/*` is set, after `ExecuteOneTurn()`, scan response content parts for image content (type=image, base64 data)
Decode the base64 image data and write raw bytes to stdout
If model config's `outputModalities` does not include `image`, fail with a clear error before the API call
If no image content part is found in the response, fail with: `"Model returned no image data. Check that the model supports image generation."`
Integration test: mock completions endpoint returns a response with a base64-encoded 1x1 PNG image content part → assert stdout contains valid PNG bytes (magic bytes `\x89PNG`)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-021. Uses chat completions API — NOT a separate images endpoint. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/output/

userStories.title: Parse audio content parts from chat completions response and emit as binary
userStories.description: As a developer, I want agent-cli to extract audio data from chat completion responses and write the raw bytes to stdout when `--output-format audio/*` is set.
acceptanceCriteria: When `--output-format audio/*` is set, after `ExecuteOneTurn()`, scan response content parts for audio content (type=audio, base64 data)
Decode base64 audio data and write raw bytes to stdout
If model config's `outputModalities` does not include `audio`, fail with a clear error before the API call
If no audio content part found in the response, fail with: `"Model returned no audio data. Check that the model supports audio generation."`
Integration test: mock completions endpoint returns response with base64 WAV audio content part → assert stdout is valid WAV (RIFF header check)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-021. Uses chat completions API — NOT a separate audio endpoint. Files: internal/agent/executor.go, internal/output/

userStories.title: Create OpenAI-compatible TTS server wrapping a local model
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an OpenAI audio API compatible HTTP server that wraps a local TTS model (e.g., Qwen3-TTS) so agent-cli can use local TTS the same way it uses cloud providers.
acceptanceCriteria: New binary or subcommand `agent tts-server` added under `cmd/agent/`
Implements `POST /v1/audio/speech` with OpenAI-compatible request schema: `{model, input, voice, speed, response_format}`
Response body is raw audio bytes (same as OpenAI TTS)
Server wraps a configurable local TTS model via its native inference API
Server is configurable via flags: `--port` (default 8080), `--model-path`, `--device` (cpu/cuda)
Manual test steps documented in `libraries/agent-cli/docs/manual-tests/tts-server.md`
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Independent of US-022/US-023. Files: cmd/agent/ (new subcommand), libraries/agent-cli/docs/manual-tests/

userStories.title: [Meta] Break down multi-session terminal visualization into implementable stories
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a detailed breakdown of the multi-session visualization feature into focused, session-sized stories so each can be implemented and verified independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Evaluate terminal UI library options (Bubble Tea vs raw ANSI vs tcell) and select one with rationale documented
Define session grouping strategy: how to associate related sessions (trace ID, parent session ID from dispatch_agent)
Define live output mechanism: how running sessions write partial output readable by the dashboard (e.g., `~/.agent-cli/sessions/<id>.live` side-channel file)

Produce follow-up stories covering: (1) live output tee in executor, (2) session list panel rendering, (3) per-session output panel, (4) keyboard navigation Ctrl+Left/Right, (5) session status indicators, (6) `agent session watch` command wiring
Each generated story has clear verifiable acceptance criteria and fits in one session
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Meta story — output is a set of new stories, not a code change. Files: libraries/agent-cli/docs/
